title: 146 skipIf silenciosos: a suite passa verde num host sem tmux em vez de falhar alto sobre dependencia ausente
description:
Medido em 2026-07-26: a suite tem 146 ocorrencias de .skipIf( distribuidas em 41 arquivos de teste, e zero ocorrencias de .skip(, .todo(, .only( ou .failing(. Na execucao completa neste host o relatorio junit registrou skipped igual a zero, ou seja todos os 146 predicados avaliaram falso porque tmux, git, bun e pgrep estao presentes na maquina. A consequencia e que num host que nao tenha alguma dessas dependencias, ate 146 testes simplesmente desaparecem da execucao e a suite reporta verde, sem nenhum sinal de que a verificacao foi parcial. Verde com buraco e indistinguivel de verde real.

Por que isso e risco e nao detalhe: o projeto ja tem cicatriz registrada dessa exata classe. O CAM-66 tratou skipIf como gate-gaming e o CAM-202 canonizou a doutrina de que gate vermelho e hard-stop e que dispensar falha como flaky, pre-existente ou ambiental e evasao proibida. Um skipIf que evapora silenciosamente e a versao estrutural do mesmo problema: em vez de um agente dispensar uma falha, a propria suite dispensa a verificacao. O CAM-186 ja mediu divergencia entre ambientes (in-container 2957 pass e 10 fail contra 3012 verdes no host), evidencia de que ambientes diferentes exercitam conjuntos diferentes de teste.

Por que agora: o repositorio e publico e o launch e o proximo marco. Um estranho que clone e rode a suite sem tmux instalado vai ver verde e concluir que verificou o produto. Para um produto cuja tese central de diferenciacao e verificacao falsificavel, uma suite que mente sobre o proprio escopo de verificacao e contradicao direta com a proposta de valor, alem de armadilha para qualquer contribuidor externo.

Direcao proposta, a validar na spec: tornar dependencia ausente um erro alto e nao um skip silencioso. Opcoes a avaliar na spec, sem escolher antecipadamente: (a) um preflight unico no inicio da suite que detecta as dependencias exigidas (tmux, git, pgrep) e falha imediatamente com mensagem acionavel listando o que falta, em vez de deixar cada arquivo decidir por conta; (b) manter o skip apenas sob um opt-in explicito e visivel, por exemplo uma variavel de ambiente deliberada, de modo que pular seja um ato consciente do operador e apareca no output; (c) fazer a contagem de testes pulados ser reportada e ratchetada, de modo que qualquer aumento de skips quebre o gate. Em todos os casos o requisito de aceitacao e o mesmo: em um host sem tmux a suite NAO pode terminar verde.

Requisitos de nao-regressao: a mudanca nao pode transformar em falha os casos legitimos onde o skip existe por razao ambiental valida e documentada; cada um dos 41 arquivos precisa ser triado para distinguir dependencia dura (ausencia deve falhar) de variacao ambiental legitima (ausencia pode pular, mas visivelmente e contabilizada). Registrar na issue a contagem final por categoria como evidencia.

Nota: esta issue nao economiza tempo de execucao e nao deve ser justificada por custo. O ganho e exclusivamente de robustez e honestidade do gate, alinhado ao ADR-0039 (o tier real-I/O existe justamente para impedir que fakes mintam) e a postura registrada em docs/agent-readiness.md de ranquear por merito de engenharia e nunca por custo operacional.

spec.scope:
Close the fully-silent verification hole in the test suite. Today `bun test` on a host without tmux drops 37 tests and still exits 0, which is indistinguishable from a real green. Replace availability-probe skipping with four things: (1) a single centralized dependency helper, (2) a suite-level preflight that fails loud and actionably when a hard dependency is missing, unless the lane explicitly declares a waiver, (3) a per-lane skip-count ratchet so any future silent skip breaks the gate, and (4) deletion of the availability probes the preflight renders dead. Two lanes must both stay honest: the HOST lane (dev machines and the macos-latest `ci` job) has every dependency, permits no waiver, and must go RED when one is missing; the CONTAINER lane (.devcontainer and the `ci-container` job, which has no tmux by design) may stay green only under a named, counted waiver.

MEASUREMENT NOTE, this spec corrects three claims in the issue text, all re-measured on main at f78f9c35. (a) The count is right: exactly 146 non-fixture `.skipIf(` occurrences across 41 files (raw grep returns 153; 7 are the guard's own fixtures). (b) The generalization is wrong: only the tmux drop is a false green. Dropping git or jq from PATH produces 37-38 HARD FAILURES alongside the skips, because a large set of equally git-dependent tests is not gated at all, so those predicates protect nothing. (c) The issue does not state the central design constraint: the container lane has no tmux by design and `scripts/test-in-container.ts` explicitly documents that a run with only skips exits 0, so a blunt fail-loud breaks that lane. The waiver mechanism exists to resolve exactly that tension.

Predicate census, measured: 72 `!gitAvailable` (24 files), 41 `!tmuxAvailable` (12 files), 31 `!jqAvailable` (2 files), 1 composite tmux+pgrep+uuidgen, 1 composite pgrep+bun+ps. There is no codex-auth, network, platform or env-var predicate anywhere in real test files: the entire surface is binary-availability probing. There is no availability helper module; every predicate is redefined inline at 45 duplicated definition sites, tmux in 3 mutually incompatible variants.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1 (centralization): a single test helper module is the ONLY place a binary-availability probe is defined. Oracle: `grep -rnE "spawnSync\('(tmux|git|jq|pgrep|ps|uuidgen)'|Bun\.which\('(tmux|git|jq)'\)" test/ --include=*.ts` returns hits only inside that helper and inside test/fixtures/version-skip-guard/**. Baseline today: 45 duplicated definition sites across 41 files, with three incompatible tmux forms (bare `spawnSync('tmux', ['-V'])`, the same with `stdio: 'pipe'`, and an IIFE+try/catch at test/integration/sendkeys-submit.test.ts:21-27).

AC2 (fail loud, the defining oracle): with every dependency present EXCEPT tmux, the suite must exit NON-ZERO with a message naming tmux. Derive the environment, never hardcode it: `BUNBIN=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$(command -v bun)")")` then `env -i HOME="$HOME" TERM="$TERM" PATH="$BUNBIN:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin" bun test; echo exit=$?`. That PATH still carries git, jq, pgrep, ps and uuidgen (all under /usr/bin or /bin) and omits only tmux. Measured on main today: `5597 pass / 37 skip / 0 fail`, exit=0. Required after the fix: exit non-zero, stderr naming the missing binary and how to install it. An exit 0 under this exact command is a FAILED acceptance criterion no matter how many tests passed.

AC3 (control, no regression): full-PATH `bun test` still reports `0 fail`, `0 skip`, exit 0, with pass count at least the 5634 baseline plus whatever this PRD adds. Additionally run the PATH-surgery inertness control: the same `env -i` line as AC2 but WITH the tmux directory prepended, derived the same way via `command -v tmux` + `readlink -f` + `dirname`. It must match the full-PATH result exactly. Both measured today at 5634 pass / 0 fail / 0 skip, so any divergence is caused by this change, not by the surgery.

AC4 (container lane under a NAMED waiver): the container lane declares its missing dependency through an explicit, visible opt-in (env var or config key), never through silent predicate evaluation. With the waiver set, the tmux-gated tests skip and the run exits 0. With the waiver NOT set inside the container, the run exits non-zero. Oracle: the in-container harness (`scripts/test-in-container.ts`) passes with the waiver and reports the skip count. This AC replaces the policy written verbatim at scripts/test-in-container.ts:12 (`// A run with only skips (fail count 0) exits 0.`) and :150 with a counted waiver.

AC5 (ratchet, demonstrated red): the expected skip count for each lane is recorded in a versioned file and asserted by the gate; any run whose skip count differs from its lane's expectation fails with a message naming the delta. Oracle, and it must actually be executed, not reasoned about: temporarily add one `test.skipIf(true)` case in a scratch test file, run the gate, observe FAILURE naming the +1 delta, then remove the scratch file and observe the gate pass. Describe both observations in the handoff. Do not commit the scratch test.

AC6 (delete the dead probes): the 72 `!gitAvailable` and 31 `!jqAvailable` gating sites are DELETED, not converted. Justification is measured, not stylistic: git and jq exist in every lane we support (git, jq, pgrep, ps and uuidgen are preinstalled on the macos-latest runner image, and .devcontainer/Dockerfile installs git and jq), and their gating is already incoherent, since dropping git from PATH yields 37-38 hard failures from ungated but equally git-dependent tests (measured Run B: 5493 pass / 103 skip / 38 fail). The predicate therefore buys nothing and advertises a git-less mode that demonstrably does not work. Oracle: `grep -rn "gitAvailable\|jqAvailable" test/ --include=*.ts` returns hits only inside the AC1 helper, if the preflight still needs those probes there.

AC7 (triage evidence): each of the 41 files is classified as hard-dependency or legitimate-environmental, and the final per-category counts are recorded in the handoff and PR body. The one site carrying a written rationale today is test/integration/orch-recycle-pid-resolve.test.ts:49-52 (`ps` is absent in oven/bun:1.2-slim, and the production recycle-watcher runs on the host, not in the container); it must remain skippable under the container waiver rather than becoming a hard failure.

AC8 (doctrine coherence): scripts/check-version-skips.ts:15-18 currently records, as deliberate policy, that capability-probe skips `remain legal` and are not flagged. That is precisely why no existing gate can catch these 146 sites. After this change the comment is false by omission and must be updated to name the preflight and ratchet as the mechanism that now governs capability probes. Oracle: the file no longer asserts capability-probe skips are ungoverned, and `bun run check:all` stays green.

AC9 (CI wiring proven, not assumed): .github/workflows/ci.yml installs tmux with `brew install tmux` before `bun run check:all`, and today nothing verifies that step worked: if it silently no-ops, CI stays green with a 37-test hole. After the fix, a tmux-less host lane must go red. State in the handoff which lane the workflow selects, and confirm the host lane sets NO waiver. Oracle: `bun run check:all` green on this machine, plus a written trace of the lane variable from workflow to preflight.
domainTerms: lane: a distinct execution environment for the suite, with its own dependency set and its own declared waiver. Two exist today, the host lane (dev machines and the macos-latest `ci` job; all dependencies present; no waiver permitted) and the container lane (.devcontainer and the `ci-container` job; tmux absent by design, since the Dockerfile installs git and jq but zero tmux).

waiver: an explicit, named, visible declaration that a lane lacks a hard dependency, replacing silent predicate evaluation. A waiver permits a specific set of tests to skip AND is counted, so the skipped set is asserted rather than merely tolerated.
ratchet: a versioned per-lane expected skip count asserted by the gate. Any deviation fails, so a newly introduced silent skip cannot enter the suite unnoticed.
false green: a suite run that exits 0 while a set of tests silently did not execute. Measured today at exactly 37 tests on an otherwise-complete host that lacks tmux.

capability probe: an inline `spawnSync(bin, ['--version'])` or `Bun.which(bin)` check whose boolean gates `test.skipIf`. All 146 sites in scope are capability probes, and scripts/check-version-skips.ts whitelists them by name.
gotchas: Do NOT modify anything under test/fixtures/version-skip-guard/** (7 files, 7 `.skipIf` occurrences, including the only `isWindows` and `!process.env['CI']` predicates in the tree). They are the fixtures for scripts/check-version-skips.ts and editing them breaks that gate. Raw `grep -roE "\.skipIf\(" test/ | wc -l` returns 153; the 146 figure in the issue is the non-fixture count and is the correct target.

THE ENVIRONMENT TRAP, this is the third-cycle-recurring defect class (CAM-398 ordering, CAM-425 session-id, CAM-420 oracle): every oracle here makes a claim about the environment it is checked in, so derive that environment, never hardcode it. The Homebrew Cellar paths measured today (/opt/homebrew/Cellar/tmux/3.6a/bin and /opt/homebrew/Cellar/bun/1.3.13/bin) are version-pinned and drift on any brew upgrade. Use `command -v` plus `readlink -f` plus `dirname`. A hardcoded path turns AC2 into a tautology the moment either tool is upgraded.

Only tmux is separable. git, jq, pgrep, ps and uuidgen all live in /usr/bin or /bin and cannot be dropped individually without creating symlinks, and creating symlinks to simulate is forbidden here (it fakes the very environment the oracle is measuring). tmux is separable only because Homebrew keeps it in its own Cellar directory. If a story needs a git-less simulation it must drop /usr/bin as a group and account for the pre-existing hard failures that appear (Run C, none of the four present: 5458 pass / 139 skip / 37 fail).

Do NOT write an acceptance criterion asserting that dropping git or jq currently produces a false green. It does not: it produces a red for the wrong reason (an unactionable pile of hard failures instead of a named missing dependency). That distinction IS the defect for those sites and is why AC6 deletes them rather than converting them.

The container lane will not exercise this change on an ordinary PR: its heavy steps run only `if: steps.changes.outputs.container_changed == 'true'`, i.e. only when .devcontainer/** or .tool-versions changed, so it is normally a neutral pass. Prove the waiver path locally with the in-container harness and say so in the handoff; a green PR is NOT evidence the container waiver works.

`bun test` prints the skip count as an `N skip` line and OMITS that line entirely when the count is zero. A ratchet parsing stdout must treat a missing line as zero, not as a parse failure, or the host lane breaks immediately.

tmux is already declared a hard runtime dependency at scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md:36 (`tmux (every session is a tmux split)`). The preflight message must enforce the documented policy, not invent a new one.

41 tmux `skipIf` sites map to only 37 skipped tests, because a few files declare the predicate more times than they gate distinct test cases. Do not treat site count and test count as interchangeable in any assertion.
